statement.p: The form of the partial fraction decomposition of a rational function is given below.

solution.p: Multiplying by the least common denominator gives 4x^{2}+2x+54 = A(x^2+9)+(Bx+C)(x - 1) Rearranging terms on the right hand side, yields 4x^{2}+2x+54 = (A+B)x^2+(-B+C)x + 9 A - C Now we equate the coefficients: \begin{array}{rl} A+B \amp = 4 \\ -B +C \amp = 2 \\ 9 A - C \amp = 54 \end{array} Solving the system gives A=6, \; B = -2 and C= 0 so the partial fraction decomposition is \frac{4x^{2}+2x+54}{(x - 1)(x^2+9)} = \frac{6}{x - 1} + \frac{-2x}{x^2+9} The definite integral is then \displaystyle \int \frac{4x^{2}+2x+54}{(x - 1)(x^2+9)} dx = 6\ln\mathopen{}\left(\left|x-1\right|\right) - 1\ln\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+9\right) +C
